questions.question: Describe what a cutting list and a sequence of manufacture contain and explain why both are prepared before any cutting begins.
questions.expected_answer: A cutting list is a table of every part needed, the quantity, its real size taken from the drawing's dimensions and the material it is cut from. A sequence of manufacture is a numbered list or flow chart of the order of work: cut all parts, assemble the base, add uprights, add braces, fit the axle and mechanism, test, with check points after each stage and a note of who does each job. They are prepared first so the team knows it has enough material, cuts identical parts together, keeps the knife in use for one short period, has everyone busy and starts work immediately.

questions.question: State the safety rules for using a craft knife, cutting and bending wire, and using a hot glue gun.
questions.expected_answer: Knife: always on a cutting mat, against a steel ruler, cutting away from the body with the holding hand behind the blade's path; several light passes, not one heavy cut; blade retracted when not in use and when carried; never catch a falling knife; replace blunt blades. Wire: cut with pliers or wire cutters, never scissors; hold the off-cut and wear eye protection; bend with pliers; fold back or tape every exposed end. Hot glue gun: hold by the handle, rest on its stand, never touch the nozzle or fresh glue; if glue touches skin run cold water over it rather than pulling it off; keep glue off the cutting mat.

questions.question: Outline the order of assembly for the PAT frame and mechanism, including how to check squareness, how to fit the axle bearings and how to test under load.
questions.expected_answer: Glue the base rails into a rectangle and check it is square by measuring both diagonals, which must be equal; let it set flat. Glue the uprights to the corners, held vertical with a set square, then the top rails. Add diagonal braces to each panel and test by pushing the top sideways. Make axle holes from the drawing before fitting uprights if possible, open them with a file or sandpaper until the dowel turns freely without wobble, and glue a card washer around each hole as a bearing. Fit the axle, pulley or gear and crank, and check the axle turns smoothly, enlarging a hole slightly if it binds. Add string or platform, then load gradually while watching for bending and opening joints, fixing problems as found and photographing each stage.
